question_text: According to drive theory, what happens after an unmet need creates internal discomfort?
hint: The drive pushes the consumer toward an action that lowers the discomfort.
correct_answer_citation: An unmet need creates an uncomfortable internal state called a drive. The drive pushes the consumer toward an action that reduces the discomfort.

options.option_text: The need disappears without any action
options.option_explanation: An unmet need continues to create tension until an action addresses it.

options.option_text: The drive pushes the consumer toward an action that reduces tension
options.option_explanation: Correct. Drive theory describes action as a way to reduce the discomfort caused by an unmet need.

options.option_text: The consumer becomes less aware of all products
options.option_explanation: Drive theory concerns tension and need satisfaction, not general attention.

options.option_text: The consumer values every product equally
options.option_explanation: Consumers still choose among options based on their goals and preferences.

question_text: Which part of expectancy theory describes the value a consumer places on the expected result?
hint: It answers the question: how much does this outcome matter to me?
correct_answer_citation: Valence is the value the consumer places on that outcome.

options.option_text: Expectancy
options.option_explanation: Expectancy is the belief that effort will lead to good performance.

options.option_text: Instrumentality
options.option_explanation: Instrumentality is the belief that good performance will lead to a desired outcome.

options.option_text: Valence
options.option_explanation: Correct. Valence is the value assigned to the expected outcome.

options.option_text: Drive reduction
options.option_explanation: Drive reduction explains how action lowers tension from an unmet need.

question_text: What makes a want become demand?
hint: Demand requires more than wanting a product.
correct_answer_citation: Demand is a want supported by both the ability and willingness to pay.

options.option_text: The consumer has both the ability and willingness to pay
options.option_explanation: Correct. A want becomes demand when purchasing power and willingness support it.

options.option_text: An advertisement repeats the product name
options.option_explanation: Repetition may increase awareness, but it does not create purchasing power.

options.option_text: The product satisfies a biological need only
options.option_explanation: Demand can involve psychological and social wants as well as biological needs.

options.option_text: The consumer sees the product in a store
options.option_explanation: Exposure does not mean the consumer is willing or able to buy.

question_text: Which example best represents an esteem need in Maslow's hierarchy?
hint: Esteem concerns achievement, respect, recognition, and status.
correct_answer_citation: Belonging and esteem needs include friendship, acceptance, achievement, and status.

options.option_text: Buying bottled water to relieve thirst
options.option_explanation: Water addresses a physiological need.

options.option_text: Installing a lock to protect a home
options.option_explanation: Home protection addresses a safety need.

options.option_text: Joining a club to make friends
options.option_explanation: Making friends addresses a belonging need.

options.option_text: Buying a watch to signal achievement
options.option_explanation: Correct. Recognition and status are examples of esteem needs.

question_text: A consumer wants both a new phone and a weekend trip, but can afford only one. What type of motivational conflict is this?
correct_answer_citation: Approach-approach conflict occurs when a consumer wants two attractive options but can choose only one.

options.option_text: Approach-approach conflict
options.option_explanation: Correct. The consumer is choosing between two desirable options.

options.option_text: Approach-avoidance conflict
options.option_explanation: This occurs when one option has both an attractive benefit and an unpleasant cost.

options.option_text: Avoidance-avoidance conflict
options.option_explanation: This occurs when every available option has an unwanted consequence.

options.option_text: Low-involvement conflict
options.option_explanation: Involvement describes the importance of a purchase, not this conflict pattern.

question_text: A buyer chooses a product mainly because it offers reliable performance and convenience. Which value is guiding the choice?
hint: This value focuses on practical results.
correct_answer_citation: Functional values focus on performance, convenience, and reliability.

options.option_text: Social value
options.option_explanation: Social value concerns belonging, recognition, and how others see the consumer.

options.option_text: Functional value
options.option_explanation: Correct. Reliability and convenience are practical functional benefits.

options.option_text: Experiential value
options.option_explanation: Experiential value focuses on pleasure, excitement, comfort, or meaning.

options.option_text: Status conflict
options.option_explanation: This is not one of the three value types introduced in the lesson.
